clue.text: Never never including the SF writer

indicators.note: the two words contain the writer's name running across them

explanation.surface: A claim that something never, ever includes a science-fiction author.
explanation.walkthrough: 'including' says the letters sit inside 'Never never': neVER NEver.
explanation.definitionFit: Jules Verne wrote early science fiction such as Twenty Thousand Leagues Under the Sea.

clue.text: Order which is offensive

explanation.surface: Asking what sort of order would cause offence.
explanation.definitionFit: A charge is a command or duty laid on someone, and a charge is also an attacking rush in battle.

clue.text: Sort of head to show benevolence

parts.note: sort means kind
a ness is a headland, a head of land jutting into the sea

explanation.surface: Some type of leader displaying goodwill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head' is a headland here: NESS appears in Scottish place names such as Loch Ness.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean goodwill shown to others, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Parts for cast to be rewritten

indicators.note: rewriting the letters of the two words puts them into a new order

explanation.surface: Roles intended for actors that need a fresh script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be rewritten' rearranges FOR and CAST together.
explanation.definitionFit: Factors are elements or components contributing to a result, so parts in that sense.

clue.text: Advertise for a title

parts.note: pro is Latin for for, as in pros and cons
a claim is a legal right or title to something

explanation.surface: Promoting something on behalf of a book or film title.
explanation.definitionFit: To advertise something is to announce or publicise it widely.

clue.text: Strain through business being dead?

parts.note: per means through or by means of
CO is short for company, a business
the late means the dead, as in the late king

explanation.surface: Stress caused by a company going under.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strain' looks like stress but is the verb meaning filter.
explanation.definitionFit: Coffee percolates when water filters slowly through the grounds, a straining action.

clue.text: New sort of latch-nice and practical

indicators.note: a new sort of the letters means they are shuffled into a fresh arrangement

explanation.surface: A novel kind of door catch that looks good and works well.
explanation.walkthrough: 'New sort of' rearranges the letters of LATCH and NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: Technical and practical both describe applied, hands-on knowledge rather than theory.

clue.text: Off colour

parts.note: feeling sick, and also one shade on the spectrum: a queasy face takes this tint

explanation.definitionFit: A nauseous person is said to look this shade, so it means unwell as well as being a colour.

clue.text: Caught and bolted a quantity of fish

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
bolted means ran off

explanation.surface: A fish that was hooked and then fled.
explanation.walkthrough: A cran is an old Scottish measure of fresh herrings, about 750 fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A cran was a measure used for landed herrings, a set volume of catch.

clue.text: Indirect arrangement to get out of debt

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word's letters gives a different order

explanation.surface: Using a roundabout scheme to clear what you owe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' reorders the letters of INDIRECT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bank account in credit has a positive balance, so its holder owes nothing.

clue.text: Much-decorated soldiers reflect on commanding officers

indicators.note: to reflect is to throw back, so the soldiers' letters are read backwards

parts.note: OR stands for other ranks, ordinary soldiers
CO stands for commanding officer, so two of them give the pair twice

explanation.surface: Highly decorated troops ponder their senior officers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reflect' turns OR into RO; 'Much-decorated' suggests medals but describes an ornate style.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is the ornate eighteenth-century style of art and architecture, heavy with ornament.

clue.text: Only requiring a couple of notes

parts.note: me is a note of the sol-fa scale
re is another note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Just needing two musical notes.
explanation.definitionFit: Mere and only both mean nothing more than, as in a mere child.

clue.text: The right quarters (with furniture) are to let

parts.note: E and N, east and north, are compass quarters
a table is a piece of furniture

explanation.surface: Furnished rooms on offer for rent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'quarters' looks like lodgings, but is two points of the compass.
explanation.definitionFit: Property described as to let is available for renting.

clue.text: When choreographed the dances must be disciplined

indicators.note: choreographing arranges steps, so these letters are rearranged into a new order

explanation.surface: Dancers made to behave once the routine is set.
explanation.walkthrough: 'When choreographed' rearranges the letters of THE DANCES.
explanation.definitionFit: Chastened means corrected and subdued, as after a punishment.

clue.text: A woman may be set about in this place

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go around the other piece
may be signals that the letters of set can be put in another order

parts.note: here means in this place

explanation.surface: A woman might be placed around here.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'set about' as a phrase meaning attack; in fact 'may be' is the anagram signal and 'about' the wrapping one.
explanation.definitionFit: Therese is a woman's given name, as in Saint Therese of Lisieux.

clue.text: Hindsight

parts.note: read as hind plus sight: a look towards the back, as in a car mirror

explanation.definitionFit: Hind means back and sight means view, so the word split in two names a view behind.

clue.text: Burn to make around a thousand

indicators.note: around means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: to make is to create
M is the Roman numeral for a thousand

explanation.surface: Setting fire to things to earn about a grand.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' puts M inside CREATE, which reads as a sum of money in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To cremate is to burn a dead body to ashes.

clue.text: Dwelling with unquiet top man

indicators.note: un- removes quiet, which is P (piano, softly in music)

parts.note: the president is the top man of a country or company

explanation.surface: A home with a restless boss in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unquiet' reads as restless but means take away P, the musical sign for quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: Resident as an adjective means living in a place, dwelling there.

clue.text: Original one — one in Latin possibly

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: in places the second one inside the reworked letters
possibly suggests the letters of Latin could take another form

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one again

explanation.surface: A first version, maybe one written in Latin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' rearranges LATIN into NTIAL, and 'in' puts I inside it after the T, all after the first I.
explanation.definitionFit: An initial step is the first, original one.

clue.text: Putting simpletons inside is criminal!

parts.note: an ass is a fool or simpleton
a second ass for the plural
in means inside

explanation.surface: Locking up fools is a crime!
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' looks like a containment signal but just gives IN after two ASSes.
explanation.definitionFit: An assassin is a murderer, a criminal killer of prominent figures.

clue.text: Cupid is sent up in some irritation

indicators.note: in a down clue, sent up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eros is the Greek counterpart of Cupid, god of love

explanation.surface: Being mocked stings the god of love somewhat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sent up' sounds like mockery; in a down answer it turns EROS upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A sore is a painful, inflamed spot on the skin, an irritation.

clue.text: Has a meal and drinks

explanation.surface: Someone dines and has a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: To sup is to eat supper, and also to sip or drink in small mouthfuls.

clue.text: Fathers hold the power, that's plain

indicators.note: hold means the first piece encloses the second

parts.note: pas are fathers, plural of pa
amp, short for ampere, is used loosely for electrical power

explanation.surface: Dads stay in charge, that's clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plain' looks like the adjective clear, but is a noun: a flat grassland.
explanation.definitionFit: The pampas are the vast treeless grasslands of South America, a level expanse.

clue.text: Swallowed many a line

parts.note: D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large number
a rank is a line, as of soldiers or taxis

explanation.surface: Lots of people fell for a story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swallowed many a line' suggests being fooled, but Swallowed is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Drank is the past tense of drink, to swallow liquid.

clue.text: A craftsman, as we say

parts.note: to aver is to declare or say firmly

explanation.surface: Asserting that someone is a craftsman, as we say.
explanation.definitionFit: A weaver makes cloth on a loom, a traditional craft.

clue.text: The main indication of fluctuation

parts.note: main is the sea, so this is the line showing how high the sea rose

explanation.definitionFit: The high-water line left on a shore shows how far the sea's level rises and falls.

clue.text: Farmers lack nothing in this country

indicators.note: lack means the farmers go without the nothing

parts.note: yeomen were small landowning farmers
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Farmers here want for nothing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lack nothing' reads as being well off, but takes O out of YEOMEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Yemen is a nation on the south of the Arabian peninsula.

clue.text: Keeps getting a man in, it's ridiculous

indicators.note: ridiculous suggests the letters are jumbled into absurd disorder

explanation.surface: Someone insists on bringing a man in, which is absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ridiculous' rearranges A MAN IN ITS.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep something up is to sustain it, a direct synonym.
